content: Before taking tetracycline, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other tetracyclines (such as doxycycline or minocycline), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. This medication may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you are sure you can perform them safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Tetracycline may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. Avoid unnecessary or prolonged sun exposure, as this medication can increase your sensitivity to sunlight. Use sunscreen and wear protective clothing when outdoors. Avoid tanning booths and sunlamps. This medication should not be used in children younger than 8 years of age because it may cause permanent tooth discoloration and other issues. Tooth discoloration has also been reported in older children and young adults. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. You should not become pregnant while using tetracycline, as it may harm an unborn baby. This medication also passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Do not start, stop, or change the dosage of any medicines without your doctor's approval. Tetracycline may interfere with certain laboratory tests, potentially causing false test results. Ensure laboratory personnel and your doctors are aware you are using this medication. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it later for another infection unless directed by your doctor. Laboratory and/or medical tests may be performed while you are taking this medication. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose. Take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Taking outdated tetracycline can result in serious illness. Tetracycline is used to treat a wide variety of bacterial infections, including acne. It is an antibiotic that works only against bacterial infections and will not be effective for viral infections (such as the common cold or flu). Take this medication by mouth on an empty stomach (at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals) as directed by your doctor, usually 2 or 4 times daily. If stomach upset occurs, ask your doctor if you can take it with food. Take each dose with a full glass of water (8 ounces or 240 milliliters) unless otherwise directed by your doctor. Do not lie down for at least 10 minutes after taking this medication. Take this medication 2 to 3 hours before or after taking any products containing aluminum, calcium, iron, magnesium, zinc, or bismuth subsalicylate. Examples include antacids, quinapril, sucralfate, vitamins/minerals, dairy products (such as milk or yogurt), and calcium-enriched juice. The dosage is based on your medical condition and response to treatment. For the best effect, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced times. Continue to take this medication until the full prescribed amount is finished, even if symptoms disappear after a few days. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, loss of appetite, mouth sores, black hairy tongue, sore throat, dizziness, headache, or rectal discomfort. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they have judged that the benefit to you is greater than the risk of side effects. Tetracycline may rarely cause increased pressure around the brain (intracranial hypertension IH). The risk of this side effect is greater for women of childbearing age who are overweight or who have had IH in the past. If IH develops, it usually resolves after tetracycline is stopped; however, there is a chance of permanent vision loss or blindness. This medication may rarely cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called C. difficile. This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new yeast infection (oral or vaginal fungal infection). A very serious allergic reaction to this drug is rare. However, seek immediate medical attention if you notice symptoms of a serious allergic reaction, including rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face/tongue/throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., call your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
